comments.text:
I respect you took the time to do this but this is a very poor comparison and very unrealistic. 

1. A realistic test would be to push it until it crackles. Not until your cpu is overloaded massively at 127%.
2. Just use something CPU limited not RAM limited. Serum + third party plugins on a track and then duplicate that track as much as you can seeing how much it can do before it becomes unstable. Eventually group every 5 tracks to be more realistic and take into account how grouping would distribute loads across cores.
3. Test single core performance as well by loading one single track only with a heavy plugin like a StandardClip with 64x oversampling and see how many instances of that plugin it can run on a single track. This is important for mastering guys who work on a one track project.

Bottom line I haven’t learned anything from this video other than the new generation is clearly better for on device AI music related stuff.

comments.text:
I respect you took the time to do this but this is a very poor comparison and very unrealistic. 

1. A realistic test would be to push it until it crackles. Not until your cpu is overloaded massively at 127%.
2. Just use something CPU limited not RAM limited. Serum + third party plugins on a track and then duplicate that track as much as you can seeing how much it can do before it becomes unstable. Eventually group every 5 tracks to be more realistic and take into account how grouping would distribute loads across cores.
3. Test single core performance as well by loading one single track only with a heavy plugin like a StandardClip with 64x oversampling and see how many instances of that plugin it can run on a single track. This is important for mastering guys who work on a one track project.

Bottom line I haven’t learned anything from this video other than the new generation is clearly better for on device AI music related stuff.
